recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Banks still cheap on average despite 2025 rally. Trading at 5-6x earnings, below book value, high dividend yields. Goldilocks environment with resilient economy, low cost of risk, favorable rate environment.
recommendations.quote: Banks are still cheap on average. So you need to be on the right side of the valuation trade.
recommendations.downside_note: Sudden change in rate or economic environment is biggest risk

recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Second/third derivative of data center trade. Need electricity for AI infrastructure. Second best performing sector in European value index.
recommendations.quote: Utilities have been seen in Europe as a second or third derivative of the data center trade, because you need a lot of electricity.

recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Next leg of value trade in 2026. Discounted pricing in negative news. German stimulus and infrastructure spending will filter through to consumer spending.
recommendations.quote: Consumer is a value sector for obvious reasons in the past, but I think this could be the next leg of the additional value push into 2026.
recommendations.position_context: Broad diversified exposure: luxury, automotive, apparel, food & beverage

recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Quality business with interesting future optionalities: truck industry dynamics, electrification, construction equipment for Ukraine rebuild.
recommendations.quote: I think it's a company that fits from its end, from its quality of business, from its end markets, some very interesting future optionalities.

recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Used to balance pro-cyclicality cheaply. Tariff fears overblown. Positive pipeline announcements on some holdings. Generic champions benefit from pricing pressure.
recommendations.quote: The pharma sector was a very interesting value sector this year because of this tariff announcement push and the over reaction of the market.
recommendations.downside_note: Pipeline risk for some companies in late decade (2030-2040)

recommendations.speaker: Andreas Wosol
recommendations.reasoning: Critical value chain for electrification - renewables, energy transmission, electricity generation. Also AI data center second derivative.
recommendations.quote: You need cables...from renewable energy, in energy transmission, in electricity generation. And funny enough, all of a sudden, it became an AI data center story as well.

insights.quote: When a certain stock, a certain sector or a certain country is big in an index, it tells you something about the past rather than about the future.
insights.summary: Index composition reflects history, not future opportunities
insights.speaker: Andreas Wosol

insights.quote: Ideally, you buy them when everyone hates them, when volumes are still negative, but you get a sense that there is an inflection point in the next 6 to 12 months in terms of volumes.
insights.summary: Buy hated stocks before volume inflection point
insights.speaker: Andreas Wosol

insights.quote: We try to be diversified across end market exposures that we think are interesting to invest in a more structural way...we don't want to have duplicated, triplicated exposure to the same end market.
insights.summary: Diversify by end markets, not just sector labels
insights.speaker: Andreas Wosol

insights.quote: The narrative-driven market that we are in for very long time, unfortunately, is a bit of a warning signal by itself. Because effectively, the narrative itself doesn't do anything.
insights.summary: Narrative-driven basket trading destroys value short-term
insights.speaker: Andreas Wosol

summary: Interview with Andreas Wosol, Head of European Equity Value at Amundi. Discussion of European value investing thesis: banks still attractive despite 2025 rally (5-6x earnings, below book), consumer sector as next value opportunity for 2026, utilities benefiting from data center demand. Emphasis on bottom-up stock picking, end market diversification, and patience in value investing.
key_takeaways: European banks still cheap despite 2025 rally, trade will continue more selectively in 2026
European consumer stocks could be next leg of value trade, supported by German stimulus
European utilities are AI/data center second derivative plays
Narrative-driven basket trading creates opportunities for fundamental investors
Diversify across end markets rather than just cyclical vs defensive labels
